selected.title: Meta says its new AI accounts have passed 10 million—what draws people in?
selected.summary: Meta reported third-quarter revenue above estimates and said its Muse AI accounts had topped 10 million. The company also disclosed a large one-time charge tied to an agreement.
selected.why_it_matters: A fast-growing feature can change how people use social platforms—and what kinds of content, privacy choices and business models platforms prioritize.
selected.challenge_question: How many Muse accounts did Meta say had been reached?
selected.answer_explanation: Meta said Muse accounts had topped 10 million. This is the company’s reported figure; it does not by itself establish how active or satisfied those users are.
selected.butterfly_question: If AI accounts become a normal part of social feeds, how could that change what people trust and share?

sources.title: Meta Q3 revenue tops estimates; Muse accounts top 10 million

selected.title: In hot-weather tournaments, changing the clock may help more than changing the date
selected.summary: A study roundup reports that adjusting tournament playing hours may increase access to lower-risk conditions more effectively than changing event dates, using environmental heat measurements to assess schedules.
selected.why_it_matters: Scheduling choices can affect athlete safety, competition fairness and event logistics as heat changes the usable hours of a day.
selected.challenge_question: According to the study summary, which change helped more with safer playing hours?
selected.answer_explanation: The study summary says adjusting playing hours had a stronger effect on available low-risk hours than changing tournament dates. The result concerns the framework studied, not every sport or venue.
selected.butterfly_question: How might heat-aware scheduling reshape the sports calendar and the way fans watch?

sources.title: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living
